subject: pathology
title: Cytokeratin, Vimentin, Desmin, Frozen Section, and FNAC

steps.tx: Intermediate filaments fingerprint cell lineage under the microscope: keratins fill epithelial cells, vimentin fills mesenchymal cells, and desmin fills muscle, so antibody panels sort carcinoma from sarcoma from lymphoma in poorly differentiated tumours. The epithelial filament family is **cytokeratin**, the first stain of the unknown tumour panel.
steps.say: Cytokeratin says epithelium, vimentin says mesenchyme, desmin says muscle; that trio opens every unknown tumour panel.

rows: Sarcoma, also melanoma and lymphoma context

steps.tx: Read this staining panel as three verdicts side by side. The first tumour colours strongly for cytokeratin, declaring epithelial lineage, the second takes vimentin instead and behaves as a sarcoma, while the third picks up desmin as a muscle tumour should. That first **cytokeratin stain** is usually the branch point of the whole undifferentiated tumour workup.
steps.say: This panel contrasts cytokeratin positive carcinoma with vimentin positive sarcoma and desmin positive muscle tumour. The cytokeratin stain is usually the first branch point in an unknown tumour workup.

vis.alt: Intermediate filament immunohistochemistry panel showing cytokeratin positive carcinoma against vimentin positive sarcoma and desmin positive muscle tumour
vis.caption: Intermediate filament immunohistochemistry panel showing cytokeratin positive carcinoma against vimentin positive sarcoma and desmin positive muscle tumour. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Keratin patterns refine the answer further: CK7 and CK20 combinations sort lung, breast, ovary, colorectal, and urothelial primaries into recognisable quadrants that guide the search for an unknown primary. Pathologists quote the pair as the **CK7 and CK20 profile** before adding lineage transcription factors.
steps.say: The CK7 and CK20 quadrant sorts most unknown primaries before a single organ specific stain is ordered.

left.title: CK7 positive, CK20 negative
points: Add TTF-1, GATA3, PAX8 to refine

right.title: CK7 negative, CK20 positive
points: CDX2 and SATB2 confirm bowel origin

steps.tx: Vimentin positivity with keratin negativity pushes a spindle cell tumour toward sarcoma, where desmin, myogenin, S100, CD34, and other markers then separate muscle, nerve sheath, vascular, and stromal families. Muscle differentiation declared by desmin and myogenin defines the **rhabdomyosarcoma panel** in childhood tumours.
steps.say: Vimentin opens the sarcoma door; desmin and myogenin then prove skeletal muscle differentiation.

vis.caption: Immunohistochemistry panels assigning lineage in a poorly differentiated neoplasm.

steps.tx: Lymphomas reject both keratin and most epithelial markers, declaring themselves with CD45 and lineage antigens, while melanoma chooses S100, SOX10, and melanocytic markers, completing the four family sort of undifferentiated tumours. The haematological gatekeeper stain is **CD45**, leukocyte common antigen.
steps.say: CD45 separates lymphoma from carcinoma, sarcoma, and melanoma in the undifferentiated tumour sort.

steps.tx: Frozen section trades permanence for speed: tissue frozen, cut, and stained within minutes answers operative questions such as margin clearance, sentinel node involvement, or whether tissue is diagnostic, accepting freeze artefact as the price. The intraoperative technique is the **frozen section**, with definitive reporting deferred to paraffin sections.
steps.say: Frozen section answers the surgeon's question in minutes; paraffin sections still deliver the definitive diagnosis.

left.title: Frozen section strengths
points: Minutes to an answer in theatre

right.title: Frozen section limits
points: Fatty and calcified tissue cuts poorly
Some diagnoses must wait for paraffin

steps.tx: Fine needle aspiration cytology draws cells through a thin needle for smears and cell blocks, diagnosing thyroid nodules, lymphadenopathy, salivary masses, and deep lesions under image guidance with minimal morbidity. Architecture is sacrificed for speed and safety in **fine needle aspiration cytology**, so some tumours still need core biopsy.
steps.say: FNAC trades architecture for speed and safety; when grading or lymphoma subtyping matters, take a core instead.

steps.tx: A multidisciplinary meeting still depends on what **fine needle aspiration cytology** can and cannot show. A thin needle draws cells for smears and cell blocks from thyroid nodules, lymph nodes, salivary masses, and deep lesions under image guidance, with little morbidity. Speed and safety are bought by giving up tissue architecture, so some tumours still need a core biopsy before the meeting can grade them or choose treatment. Discussion does not restore structure the needle never collected.
steps.say: Fine needle aspiration takes cells rather than intact architecture from thyroid nodules, nodes, salivary masses, and deep lesions, and it does so with little morbidity. When grade or lymphoma subtype matters, the meeting still needs a core biopsy.

vis.alt: Clinicians review aspiration cytology slides together in a multidisciplinary meeting.
vis.caption: Cytology slides from a thin needle sample are reviewed by several specialties before a treatment plan is chosen. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Cytology grading systems convert smears into decisions: Bethesda categories for thyroid and cervix translate microscopic impressions into repeat, surgery, or observation pathways shared across teams. Standardised vocabularies protect patients from idiosyncratic reports; the thyroid system is the **Bethesda system**. Bethesda reporting also transformed cervical cytology into a shared international language for screening programmes.
steps.say: Bethesda categories turn cytology words into shared decisions about repeat sampling, surgery, or observation.

steps.tx: Choosing among FNAC, core, frozen, and excision is a clinical decision balancing urgency, architecture, risk, and what the answer will change, made jointly by clinician, radiologist, and pathologist. Triple assessment in breast disease models the teamwork; the organising forum is the **multidisciplinary team meeting**.
steps.say: Pick the biopsy that answers the management question; the multidisciplinary meeting exists to make that choice well.

vis.caption: Breast cancer assessment, where cytology, core biopsy, and immunohistochemistry combine in triple assessment.
